status: VERIFIED - 2026-08-26 built host-side from the CC0 Dataverse deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/VUKNOQ, Experiment2.dta): 6,079 respondents, 3 treatment arms (n 1,471-1,541) + pure placebo control (n 1,575); five scales rebuilt exactly per ReplicationCode.do including mean imputation and missingness caps; diff-in-means effects consistent with the paper's '~0.1 SD on each primary scale, p<.05' summary
sample_description: 6,079 U.S. adults, NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE YouGov panel (matched-and-weighted design; analysis here unweighted), fielded mid-July to early August 2020. Each respondent was randomised to read ONE of three COVID-19 messages or a PLACEBO text about bird feeding with no COVID content, then immediately answered the outcome battery. All outcomes are means of 0-1 items, reported on their 0-1 range. Effects are vs the PLACEBO control, so unlike Experiment 1 they include the value of the basic information itself; the paper reports roughly 0.1 SD effects for the two persuasive messages on the primary scales. Note the timing: July-August 2020, when masking guidance was established and distancing was politicized.

e2_normsbeliefs.question: BELIEFS scale, mean of 3 agreement items (0-1): distancing stops me getting sick; stops others getting sick; I would feel guilty if I did not distance.

e2_distancing.question: DISTANCING scale, 16 items (0-1): likely to practice distancing, would self-isolate if exposed, would alert authorities if positive, plus 13 reverse-coded willingness-to-do-activities items (church, library, elective medical care, family's/friend's house inside, protest, public transport, airplane, work outside home, small/large meetings inside/outside).

e2_food.question: FOOD scale, 4 reverse-coded items (0-1): willingness to go to a coffee shop, eat inside a restaurant, eat outside at a restaurant, go to a bar.

e2_others.question: OTHERS/peer scale, 8 items (0-1): persuade others, report a violating business, non-compliers are selfish, would cooperate with contact tracing, and reverse-coded non-compliers trustworthy / likeable / competent / intelligent.

e2_masks.question: MASKS scale, 7 items (0-1): likelihood of wearing a mask at work, on public transport, walking outside, shopping, visiting a friend, in a park, plus preference for a mask-requiring store over a mask-banning store.

message_texts.Placebo control (bird feeding): [Reference group.] A placebo text about backyard bird feeding, containing no information about COVID-19 or risk reduction.
message_texts.Baseline Information: To end the COVID-19 pandemic, public health officials believe we should practice social distancing. Social distancing means that you should: Avoid gatherings of any size outside your household, such as a friend's house, parks, restaurants, shops, or any other place. Work from home when possible. Stay at least 6 feet away from others if you need to go out in public, for example to shop for food or medicine. Also consider covering your mouth and nose with a cloth face covering when around others, including when you have to go out in public. Avoid using any kind of public transportation, ridesharing, or taxis, if possible.
message_texts.Protect Others - Linear Cooperation: [The baseline information text, followed by:] Stopping COVID-19 is important because it reduces the risk that members of your family and community could get sick and die. COVID-19 kills people of all ages. Even for those who are young and healthy, there is a risk of death or long-term disability. Many other people are already social distancing. Remember, every person who practices social distancing reduces the risk that people you care about get sick. While you can't do it alone, we can all protect everyone by working together.
message_texts.Reframing Bravery: Soldiers, fire fighters, EMTs, and doctors are putting their lives on the line to serve others during the COVID-19 pandemic. That's bravery. But people who don't practice social distancing because they don't think they will get sick or aren't worried aren't brave, they are reckless. By not social distancing, you are risking the health of your family, friends, and community. There is nothing attractive and independent-minded about ignoring public health guidance to practice social distancing. Not social distancing means you risk the health of others. To show strength practice social distancing so you don't get sick and take resources from other people who need them more, or risk spreading the disease to those who are at risk. Social distancing may be inconvenient, but it works.

provenance.source: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/VUKNOQ (CC0 1.0); paper doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0264782. Stimuli transcribed verbatim from the paper's Table 1; the placebo is described in the paper, its text is not reproduced there.
provenance.scales: rebuilt exactly per ReplicationCode.do: reverse-coding, mean imputation of missing items, and the scale-level missingness caps (distancing needs >=12 of 16 items, food >=3 of 4, peers >=6 of 8, masks all 7, beliefs all 3)
caveats: July-August 2020: masking established, distancing politicized; effects vs a true no-information placebo
n~1,500/arm gives per-cell SEs of 0.7-1.0 pp - levels and directions are well measured, but only 3 arms per outcome
party derived from D_newpid7 (1-3 Dem, 4 Ind, 5-7 Rep); gender from D_gender (1 Male, 2 Female); age_band keeps YouGov's five numeric codes 1-5 (youngest to oldest) as strings
analysis unweighted (the deposit's weights are not used), matching the replication code's regressions

exclude_from_slope: jointly-held-out head-to-head task (2026-08-26): scored once by idea_01's frozen predictor for the idea_01-vs-idea_02 comparison; must never enter any idea_01 calibration fit
